front: Why do living things need nitrogen?
back: To make amino acids and proteins (and DNA).
notes: Plants absorb nitrate ions; animals eat proteins.

back: Converting nitrogen gas from the air into nitrogen compounds (ammonium compounds), by nitrogen-fixing bacteria or lightning.
Free in the soil, and in the root nodules of legumes (groundnuts, soya beans, cowpeas, round nuts).

front: What do decomposers produce from dead proteins and urea?

back: Conversion of ammonium ions into nitrate ions (via nitrite) by nitrifying bacteria; needs oxygen.
Conversion of nitrate ions into nitrogen gas by denitrifying bacteria, mainly in waterlogged soils.
Removal of the nitrogen-containing part of excess amino acids in the liver, forming urea.
Its energy makes nitrogen and oxygen combine; the oxides dissolve in rain and reach the soil as nitrates.

front: Why rotate maize with groundnuts or soya beans?
back: Legume nodules fix nitrogen; their decaying roots and residues add nitrate for the next maize crop.

front: Why do waterlogged soils lose nitrate?
back: Little oxygen: denitrifying bacteria thrive and nitrifying bacteria (which need oxygen) slow down.
